history.sg_progress: The Business Transformation and Accountability Division has already enhanced its focus on the use of low-value acquisitions as part of its ongoing efforts to strengthen the delegation of authority monitoring framework. As noted by the Board in paragraph 343 of its report, the Division introduced a key performance indicator in 2023 to enable more targeted monitoring and outreach as a second line of defence. Paragraph 345 of the Board’s report further highlights a reduction in the number of low-value acquisitions and blanket purchase orders in 2024 compared with 2023. The Board also acknowledges that a pilot response mechanism for low-value acquisitions was under way at the time of the audit, aimed at deepening understanding of the use of low-value acquisitions and informing follow-up actions in both the first and second lines of defence. To further strengthen monitoring as the first line of defence, the Division will issue a guide to monitoring low-value acquisitions, which will outline the monitoring process, the recommended frequency and analytical procedures, and appropriate action in response to monitoring results.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration strengthen efforts to monitor the improper use of low-value acquisitions and blanket purchase orders by closely following up on and adopting a more targeted approach in the pilot response mechanisms in order to reduce the improper use thereof.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Business Transformation and Accountability Division enhanced quarterly monitoring and adopted a risk-based mechanism to tackle cases of irregular low-value acquisitions. Based on 2023–2025 data analysis, it targeted seven high-risk entities accounting for 70% of improper usage of low-value acquisitions. The Business Transformation and Accountability Division engaged with those entities directly, supplying data, templates and tracking tools to low- value acquisition focal points for evidence-based follow-up, policy clarification and corrective action. It also released a low-value acquisitions monitoring guide on the Knowledge Gateway to support all entities. Combined monitoring and targeted interventions delivered clear improvements: cases of improper low- value acquisitions dropped by 55% in the first quarter of 2026 versus the fourth quarter of 2025. Improper use of blanket purchase orders remained minimal, with no cases in the final three quarters of 2025 and only two in the first quarter of 2026. Relevant operational lessons have been documented to strengthen delegation of authority oversight.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Business Transformation and Accountability Division strengthened its regular quarterly monitoring by implementing in parallel a risk-based response mechanism to address the identified issues, and that initial results demonstrate measurable progress resulting from the combined effect of regular quarterly monitoring and the targeted response mechanism, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
